title: Burn injury
reference: NASA Flight Medicine Clinical Practice Guidelines: Thermal & Chemical Burn Management in Microgravity.

q1.text: Is the burn chemical (battery acid, toxic propellant, ammonia coolant) rather than thermal?

i_chem.text: CHEMICAL BURN DECONTAMINATION: Don protective nitrile gloves. Remove contaminated clothing immediately into sealed hazardous disposal bag. Flush skin with copious sterile water.

t_chem_flush.text: Flush affected area continuously with sterile water for 15 minutes. Use liquid vacuum to capture free-floating water globules.

q2.text: Is there facial involvement, singed nasal hairs, soot in mouth, or hoarseness (signs of thermal inhalation injury)?

i_inhalation.text: CRITICAL AIRWAY INHALATION BURN: High risk of rapid laryngeal edema. Don high-flow humidified O2 mask immediately. Prepare endotracheal intubation kit at bedside.

q3.text: Is the burn deep (full-thickness, white/charred, insensitive to touch) or covering >10% of total body surface area?

i_severe_thermal.text: SEVERE THERMAL BURN: Apply sterile non-adherent Water-Jel burn sheets. Do not apply ice or grease. Start IV access in unburned limb and initiate Parkland fluid calculation.

t_burn_cool.text: Maintain sterile cooling compresses for 10 minutes while monitoring patient body temperature to avoid hypothermia.

i_minor_burn.text: SUPERFICIAL / MINOR BURN: Cool area with sterile water compresses for 5 minutes. Apply thin layer of Bacitracin ointment and dress with sterile non-stick hydrogel bandage.

q_airway.text: Is the skin decontamination complete and does the patient exhibit any chemical vapors inhalation symptoms?

i_chem_inhale.text: Administer supplemental O2 and nebulized bronchodilators; monitor for systemic chemical toxicity.

end_chem_ok.text: Chemical burn washed thoroughly. Apply protective soothing dressing and record chemical agent identifier.

end_monitor.text: Minor burn managed successfully. Administer oral analgesics (Ibuprofen / Acetaminophen) as needed; check dressing daily.

end_escalate.text: SEVERE BURN ESCALATION: Flight Surgeon notified. High risk of fluid shift, hypovolemic shock, and infection in closed environment.
